questions.stem: Consider this: A detective questioning a suspect obtains a confession after custodial questioning. The suspect was not under arrest. Which statement best states the governing legal rule on these facts?

options.text: Warnings are required only after a formal arrest is announced on these facts.
options.misconception: treats arrest as the only trigger

options.text: Any interview at a police station is custodial regardless of the circumstances on these facts.
options.misconception: confuses custody with the station house

options.text: Warnings are required before questioning when a suspect is in custody, meaning a reasonable person would not feel free to leave and the setting has the coercive pressure of formal arrest on these facts.
Every conversation between an officer and a citizen must begin with warnings on these facts.
options.misconception: assumes any questioning requires warnings

questions.explanation: The trigger is custodial interrogation, not simply questioning. The inquiry asks how a reasonable person would understand the setting, and it focuses on the pressure created by the interview rather than the label attached to it. Here the decisive point is when custody triggers the warning requirement, so the result follows from that doctrine rather than from the surface appeal of a competing statement. Each distractor rests on a different mistake about how the doctrine operates.
questions.hint: Ask whether a reasonable person would have felt free to end the encounter. Keep the inquiry on when custody triggers the warning requirement.
